name: Greetings & basics
description: The phrases you say twenty times a day. All polite register.

examples.ja: おはようございます。今日もいい天気ですね。
examples.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. kyou mo ii tenki desu ne.
examples.en: Good morning. Nice weather again today.

cards.tip: ohayou is the greeting; gozaimasu is the polite verb ending that lifts it to formal. Casual: ohayou. Morning only, roughly before 10 or 11.

examples.ja: こんにちは、はじめまして。

cards.tip: Set greeting from midday on. The final wa is the topic particle は, which is why it is written は but said wa. Neutral register, no casual/formal split.
Evening counterpart of konnichiwa, same wa ending and same neutral register.

cards.ja: ありがとうございます

examples.ja: 手伝ってくれて、ありがとうございます。
どうもありがとうございます。

cards.tip: arigatou (thank you) + gozaimasu (polite ending). Casual: arigatou, or just doumo. Past tense arigatou gozaimashita thanks for something already finished.

cards.en: Excuse me / Sorry (to get attention or apologise)

examples.ja: すみません、駅はどこですか。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

examples.ja: すみません、お水をください。

cards.tip: Polite set phrase that covers apology, getting attention, and thanks-for-your-trouble. Casual: gomen. Stretch it (sumimaseeen) to call a waiter.
gomen (sorry) + nasai (a soft command ending). Warmer and more personal than sumimasen; for when you actually did something. Casual: gomen or gomen ne.

examples.ja: はじめまして、ベンです。
examples.en: Nice to meet you, I'm Ben.

cards.tip: From hajimeru (to begin): literally 'for the first time'. Said once at a first meeting, any register.

cards.ja: よろしくお願いします
cards.en: Please treat me well / Pleased to work with you

examples.ja: ベンです。よろしくお願いします。
examples.en: I'm Ben. Pleased to meet you.

cards.tip: yoroshiku (well, favourably) + onegaishimasu (I request). Closes an introduction; also 'please take care of it' when handing something over. Casual: yoroshiku.

examples.ja: チェックイン、お願いします。

cards.tip: o- (honorific prefix) + negai (wish) + shimasu (do, polite). Any noun + onegaishimasu is a complete polite request. Casual: onegai.
Yes, but also 'I'm listening' and 'here you go'. Formal and casual alike. un is the casual yes.
Polite no, also 'don't mention it' after thanks. Casual: uun or iya. Japanese often avoids a flat no; chotto... is the softer refusal.

cards.en: It's fine / I'm okay / No thanks
cards.tip: daijoubu (okay, fine) is a na-adjective; desu is the polite copula, 'is'. Drop desu for casual. Rising tone makes it a question. Also a polite 'no thanks'.
Past polite form of wakaru (to understand). Past tense signals 'got it, done'. Casual: wakatta.

cards.en: I don't understand / I don't know

examples.ja: すみません、よくわかりません。

cards.tip: -masen is the polite negative ending of a verb: wakaru → wakarimasen. Casual: wakaranai.

cards.ja: 日本語が少しわかります
cards.tip: nihongo (Japanese) + ga (subject particle) + sukoshi (a little) + wakarimasu (understand). wakaru takes ga, not o.

cards.ja: もう一度お願いします

examples.ja: すみません、もう一度お願いします。

cards.tip: mou (again, more) + ichido (one time) + onegaishimasu (please). Any noun phrase + onegaishimasu is a request.

cards.ja: ゆっくりお願いします
cards.tip: yukkuri (slowly) is an adverb. Add it to any request: yukkuri hanashite kudasai, please speak slowly.
eigo (English) + o (object particle) + hanasemasu (can speak, potential form of hanasu) + ka (question marker). ka turns any polite sentence into a question with no word-order change.

cards.en: Excuse me (entering or leaving a room)
cards.tip: shitsurei (rudeness) + shimasu (I do): 'I'm being rude', said when entering, leaving, or hanging up. Past tense shitsurei shimashita apologises for something already done.

cards.en: Thanks for your hard work (greeting among coworkers)
cards.tip: o- + tsukare (tiredness) + sama (honorific) + desu. 'You must be tired' as appreciation. Workplace greeting and goodbye; reply with the same. Casual: otsukare.
Formal farewell that implies a long absence. In daily life use ja mata, mata ashita, or shitsurei shimasu.
ja (well then) + mata (again). Casual. Polite version: dewa mata. mata ashita = see you tomorrow.
